title: Nutrient amendment records from the Dava meadows
public_context: Field nutrient studies often compare amended plots with untreated controls, sometimes across several sites. Plot assignment, baseline differences, weather, and the choice of response measure all affect what a comparison can support. A response at one site may not transfer to another, especially when soil and drainage conditions differ.
source_text:
The Dava meadow study compared low-dose phosphorus additions at three fenced sites: Alder Flat, Reed Rise, and the south margin of Kestrel Pool. At each site, four plots received a measured granule application and four nearby plots received no granules. The plots were paired by slope position, but the pairs were not randomized because the field crew had to avoid old drainage lines and rabbit burrows. The application was made once, in late May, before the main flowering period.

Soil samples collected in April showed that Alder Flat had the highest background phosphorus, while Reed Rise had the most compacted surface soil. Kestrel Pool had the shallowest water table during the spring visit. The report keeps those baseline descriptions in its site table and cautions against treating the three locations as interchangeable replicates. The same dose was used at each site, but no attempt was made to equalize soil retention or drainage.

By August, the treated Alder Flat plots had more flowering stems of the common marsh sedge than their paired controls. Reed Rise showed a smaller difference, and Kestrel Pool showed no consistent treated-control pattern across its four pairs. The report gives the paired counts rather than only a pooled average. It also records that a storm overtopped one Kestrel plot marker in June; the crew restored the marker but could not tell whether granules moved beyond the plot boundary.

The authors do not claim that phosphorus caused the Alder Flat difference. They note that the same plots were selected partly for access, and that no pre-application flowering count was made. Nor did the study measure seed production or next-year recruitment; flowering stems were the only plant response used in its summary table. A short note says the pattern is consistent with a nutrient response at Alder Flat, while leaving seasonal and site-selection explanations open.

For the following year, the team proposes marking new plots outside the drainage lines, recording baseline stems before application, and adding a low-phosphorus site if access can be arranged. It recommends keeping the storm-affected Kestrel pair in the archive but showing its status separately in any site summary. The report says that a second application is not yet scheduled. It offers no estimate of how long a one-time dose remains available in each soil, and it does not recommend a basin-wide application on the basis of this season alone.
authoring_note: The dossier contrasts paired within-site responses against nonrandom assignment and unequal site baselines, with a storm creating a localized treatment-boundary uncertainty.

supported_claims.claim: Each of three sites had four granule-treated plots and four nearby untreated plots, paired by slope but not randomized.
evidence: At each site, four plots received a measured granule application and four nearby plots received no granules. The plots were paired by slope position, but the pairs were not randomized because the field crew had to avoid old drainage lines and rabbit burrows.

supported_claims.claim: The three sites differed in measured background phosphorus, compaction, and water-table depth.
evidence: Soil samples collected in April showed that Alder Flat had the highest background phosphorus, while Reed Rise had the most compacted surface soil. Kestrel Pool had the shallowest water table during the spring visit.

supported_claims.claim: By August, treated Alder Flat plots had more marsh sedge flowering stems than paired controls.
evidence: By August, the treated Alder Flat plots had more flowering stems of the common marsh sedge than their paired controls.

supported_claims.claim: Reed Rise had a smaller difference and Kestrel Pool had no consistent pattern across its four pairs.
evidence: Reed Rise showed a smaller difference, and Kestrel Pool showed no consistent treated-control pattern across its four pairs.

supported_claims.claim: A storm overtopped one Kestrel plot marker and possible granule movement beyond the plot could not be determined.
evidence: It also records that a storm overtopped one Kestrel plot marker in June; the crew restored the marker but could not tell whether granules moved beyond the plot boundary.

supported_claims.claim: The study used flowering stems as its only plant response and did not measure seed production or recruitment.
evidence: Nor did the study measure seed production or next-year recruitment; flowering stems were the only plant response used in its summary table.

explicit_negatives.claim: The authors do not claim that phosphorus caused the Alder Flat difference.
evidence: The authors do not claim that phosphorus caused the Alder Flat difference.

explicit_negatives.claim: The report does not recommend a basin-wide application based on this season alone.
evidence: It offers no estimate of how long a one-time dose remains available in each soil, and it does not recommend a basin-wide application on the basis of this season alone.

licensed_inferences.claim: The observed Alder Flat pattern is compatible with a phosphorus response but does not identify phosphorus as its cause.
licensed_inferences.rationale: A treated-control difference was observed, but plots were not randomized, there was no baseline stem count, and the authors explicitly leave selection and seasonal explanations open.

licensed_inferences.claim: A pooled three-site effect could conceal substantial site-specific variation and the boundary uncertainty at Kestrel Pool.
licensed_inferences.rationale: Site baselines and response patterns differ, while one Kestrel marker was overtopped and movement beyond its boundary is unresolved.

unspecified_probes.neutral_question: Which brand of phosphorus granule did the crew apply?
unspecified_probes.presupposition_question: Did the crew apply Northbank 12 granules at all three sites?
unspecified_probes.candidate_claim: Northbank 12 granules were applied at all three sites.
unspecified_probes.boundary_note: The report specifies measured granules and one dose but gives no product name or formulation.

unspecified_probes.neutral_question: How many millimetres of rain fell at Alder Flat during July?
unspecified_probes.presupposition_question: Did Alder Flat receive 42 millimetres of rain during July?
unspecified_probes.candidate_claim: Alder Flat received 42 millimetres of rain in July.
unspecified_probes.boundary_note: The only described weather event is a June storm at Kestrel; the report supplies no July rainfall total for Alder Flat.

unspecified_probes.neutral_question: What factors, if any, explain Alder Flat's treated-control difference?
unspecified_probes.presupposition_question: Was the Alder Flat treated-control difference entirely due to access-related plot selection rather than phosphorus?
unspecified_probes.candidate_claim: The Alder Flat treated-control difference was entirely due to access-related plot selection rather than phosphorus.
unspecified_probes.boundary_note: The report says plots were partly selected for access and leaves selection and seasonal explanations open; it does not identify either as the full cause.

consistency_questions.question: Why does the Alder Flat difference support a limited response interpretation rather than a causal conclusion?
consistency_questions.reference_answer: The treated plots had more stems, but nonrandom pairing and the absence of baseline stem counts leave selection and seasonal explanations unresolved; the authors do not claim causation.

consistency_questions.question: How should the Kestrel result be represented alongside the cross-site comparison?
consistency_questions.reference_answer: Kestrel's inconsistent pairs and storm-overtopped marker should remain visible as a site-specific qualification; the sites also differ in their baseline conditions.
